items.question: What auspicious deception of time does the speaker now wish to hear explained?
premises: The speaker asks to hear now.
items.inference: The verse frames time's deception as a desirable teaching to be heard.
uncertainties: Whether śubham modifies vañcanaṃ or the whole request.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear the auspicious deception of time.

items.question: How is death destroyed without doubt according to the teaching being given?
premises: Death is destroyed in the stated manner.
items.inference: The verse assures that the method removes death with certainty.
uncertainties: The exact method is supplied in following verses.
items.plain_english: I tell you without doubt: thus death is destroyed.

items.question: What happens to even a wise person when nectar's tip burns with the essence of juice?
premises: The essence of juice acts upon it.
items.inference: The verse warns that subtle nectar can burn even the wise.
uncertainties: Whether dahyamāna describes the nectar or the person.
items.plain_english: Even a wise person is burned at the tip of nectar by the essence of juice.

items.question: How should air be drunk after placing it at the root of tongue and palate?
premises: Air is placed at tongue-palate root.

items.plain_english: Having placed air at the root of tongue and palate, one should drink it slowly.

items.question: What happens to old age and death when this practice is done for one year?
premises: Old age and death are destroyed.
items.inference: The verse promises destruction of aging and death after one year of practice.

items.plain_english: When practiced for one year, old age and death are destroyed.

items.question: Does poison enter the body even when one is bitten by great serpents?
premises: Poison does not enter the body.
items.inference: The verse claims immunity to poison even from great serpent bites.
uncertainties: Whether daṃśito is passive participle or adjective.
items.plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one is bitten by great serpents.
